blocks.text: The chapter resolves a concern about inherited land passing from one tribe to another through marriage. Moses affirms the concern raised by the leaders of Gilead: Zelophehad’s daughters may choose their husbands, but they must marry within their father’s tribe. Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah comply, so their inheritance remains within Manasseh. The closing verse locates these commands on the plains of Moab, the endpoint of Numbers’ geographical movement from Sinai through Kadesh and the Transjordan. Egypt remains the land remembered as left behind rather than the book’s principal narrative setting.

Numbers 36 completes a larger section in which the new generation is prepared to receive the land. Across Numbers 26–36, that preparation includes a second census, inheritance rulings, Joshua’s commission, land boundaries, towns, and safeguards concerning tribal property. The ruling about Zelophehad’s daughters is therefore part of an extended body of arrangements governing Israel’s anticipated inheritance.
